title: Indonesia | OJK Bank IT, Cyber Resilience and Data Protection
tagline: Apply POJK 11/2022, PADK 1/2026 and SEOJK 29/2022: security awareness, cyber resilience, incident reports to OJK and data secrecy.
sectors: IT service providers serving Indonesian banks
Bank contractors and consultants with system access
description:
This quest teaches the information technology, cyber security and data rules that the Financial Services Authority (Otoritas Jasa Keuangan, OJK) sets for conventional commercial banks in Indonesia. It is based on **OJK Regulation (POJK) 11/POJK.03/2022** on the use of information technology by commercial banks, **OJK Board Member Regulation (PADK) 1 of 2026** on IT operation by commercial banks (in force 1 March 2026), **OJK Circular (SEOJK) 29/SEOJK.03/2022** on cyber resilience and security, the bank secrecy articles of the Banking Law as amended by **Law 4 of 2023 (the P2SK Law)**, and, in general terms, **Law 27 of 2022 on Personal Data Protection**.

PADK 1/2026 expects the security policy to include training and an awareness programme and requires security training or briefings for employees, consultants, temporary staff and IT provider staff according to their roles. SEOJK 29/2022 expects a cyber awareness programme at least once a year, checked by phishing simulation at least yearly. This quest supports those duties for all staff, with deeper material for IT, risk, cyber and data protection teams.

In five stages at a fictional Indonesian bank you cover IT governance, people and access, cyber resilience, incident reporting to OJK, providers and disaster recovery, and secrecy, personal data and audit readiness.

The quest builds knowledge and does not replace your bank's own information security, IT and data protection policies; always follow them and the current official OJK texts.
audience: All employees of conventional commercial banks in Indonesia who need yearly security and cyber awareness
Consultants, temporary staff and IT service provider staff with access to bank systems or information
IT operations, IT risk, cyber security and incident response teams
Data protection, compliance and legal staff who handle customer data and bank secrecy
Directors, commissioners and IT steering committee members who oversee IT and cyber risk
outcomes: Explain how POJK 11/2022, PADK 1/2026 and SEOJK 29/2022 fit together and who is accountable for bank IT
Apply PADK 1/2026 controls on the security policy, role-based training, screening, confidentiality and access
Describe the cyber resilience processes, yearly cyber ratings, security testing and awareness expectations
Report significant IT and cyber incidents to OJK on time and oversee IT providers and disaster recovery
Protect depositor secrecy and personal data and keep the audit, report and training evidence OJK expects

sessions.title: OJK's IT Rulebook: POJK 11/2022, PADK 1/2026 and IT Governance
sessions.summary: Learn how POJK 11/2022, PADK 1/2026 and SEOJK 29/2022 fit together, who is accountable for IT at a bank, where systems must sit, and how OJK sanctions IT breaches.
objectives: Explain how POJK 11/2022, PADK 1/2026 and SEOJK 29/2022 relate and when each took effect
Describe the IT roles of directors, commissioners, the IT steering committee, the IT unit and the cyber unit
Apply the data-location rules for data centres, DR centres and transaction processing
Describe OJK's two-step administrative sanction ladder for IT breaches

cards.title: Day one in the cyber security unit
cards.setting: Cyber Resilience and Security Unit, Bank Lintas Kepulauan head office, Jakarta. Monday, 8:15 am.

lines.text: You have just joined Bank Lintas Kepulauan, a fictional conventional commercial bank with branches from Medan to Jayapura, as an analyst in its cyber resilience and security unit.
Welcome! I'm Andreas Wijaya, head of the unit. Your timing is perfect: OJK's new board member regulation on bank IT took effect on 1 March 2026 and our self-check against it starts today.
Nur Aini Hasibuan, IT risk, Medan. I keep hearing three names: POJK 11, PADK 1 and SEOJK 29. Which one actually binds us, and which one tells us how?
Made Wirawan, IT operations and the data centre. I just want to know who signs off when something breaks. Last month our IT steering committee met without the risk director.
Yohanes Kambu, branch operations, Makassar. And my tellers ask why they must sit security training every year when they never touch a server.
Larasati Putri, data protection, compliance. Add one more question: who explains to OJK if a vendor leaks customer data?
Five questions, one mission. Stage one is the Rulebook Tower: learn the layers of OJK's IT rules, who is accountable for what, and what happens when a bank falls short.

cards.title: Three layers of OJK's bank IT rules

scenes.heading: The regulator
scenes.narration: Otoritas Jasa Keuangan, the Financial Services Authority known as OJK, licenses and supervises Indonesia's commercial banks. Its binding regulations are called POJK.

scenes.heading: The regulation
scenes.narration: POJK 11 of 2022 on the use of information technology by commercial banks was promulgated on 7 July 2022 and took effect three months later. It replaced the 2016 IT risk regulation and its 2020 amendment.

scenes.heading: The detailed guide
scenes.narration: PADK 1 of 2026, a regulation of an OJK board member, implements POJK 11. It was set on 23 January 2026, took effect on 1 March 2026 and revoked the old 2017 IT risk circular, SEOJK 21.

scenes.heading: The cyber circular
scenes.narration: SEOJK 29 of 2022, an OJK circular dated 27 December 2022, sets out how banks keep cyber resilience and security: risk ratings, maturity, testing, the cyber unit and cyber incident reports.

scenes.heading: How they fit
scenes.narration: POJK 11 states the duties and sanctions. PADK 1 explains how to run IT governance, security, providers and data. SEOJK 29 covers the cyber side. Read them together.

cards.title: The rule stack you work under
cards.caption: Higher layers set the duty; lower layers explain how to meet it. Your bank's policy must fit all of them.

items.label: Banking Law and P2SK Law
items.detail: Statutes: bank secrecy, OJK's powers and criminal penalties.

items.label: POJK 11/2022
items.detail: Binding duties on IT governance, security, cyber, providers, data, audit and reports.

items.label: PADK 1/2026
items.detail: Detailed guide for IT operation, in force 1 March 2026; revoked SEOJK 21/2017.

items.label: SEOJK 29/2022
items.detail: Cyber resilience and security: ratings, testing, cyber unit, incident reports.

items.label: Bank policies and procedures
items.detail: Your bank's own security policy, standards and procedures.

cards.title: Who does what in IT governance
cards.prompt: Match each party to its duty under POJK 11/2022.

pairs.right: Sets the IT strategic plan and IT policies and monitors all IT activity.
Evaluates, directs and monitors the IT strategic plan and IT governance.
Recommends to directors on IT strategy, policies, projects, costs and resources.
Plans, builds, operates and monitors IT as the directors direct.
Handles cyber resilience and stays independent of IT management.

cards.question: Which instrument took effect on 1 March 2026 and revoked SEOJK 21/2017?
options: PADK 1 of 2026 on IT operation by commercial banks
POJK 11 of 2022 on the use of IT by commercial banks
SEOJK 29 of 2022 on cyber resilience and security
cards.explanation: PADK 1/2026, set by an OJK board member on 23 January 2026, took effect on 1 March 2026 and revoked SEOJK 21/2017. POJK 11/2022 is the parent regulation from July 2022, and SEOJK 29/2022 remains the cyber circular.

cards.title: What POJK 11/2022 requires of every bank
cards.body:
POJK 11/2022 applies to every commercial bank in Indonesia, including branches of foreign banks. Its core duties:

- **Good IT governance** across both IT managers and IT users, mapping business processes, structure, policies, **supporting people** and **IT culture** (Articles 2-3).
- Clear **authority and responsibility** for directors, commissioners and officers at every level (Article 4).
- An **IT steering committee** chaired by a director, with at least the IT director, the risk director and the heads of the IT and user units (Article 7).
- An **IT unit** and an **IT strategic plan**, sent to OJK by the end of November before the plan period (Articles 8, 12-13).
- **Risk management**, **information security** across people, process, technology and the physical environment, and a tested **disaster recovery plan** (Articles 15-18).
- **Cyber resilience** and an independent cyber unit (Articles 21-26).
- Rules on **IT service providers**, data location, **data and personal data**, internal audit and **reporting**.

cards.title: OJK's sanction ladder for IT breaches
cards.caption: The same two-step ladder appears throughout POJK 11/2022, for example in Articles 9, 20, 27 and 46.

items.label: Breach found
items.detail: OJK finds a bank in breach of a listed POJK 11 duty.

items.label: Written warning
items.detail: The first administrative sanction is a written reprimand.

items.label: Still not fixed
items.detail: The bank has been warned but has not met the duty.

items.label: Heavier sanctions
items.detail: A ban on new products, a freeze on certain activities and/or a lower governance score in the soundness rating.

cards.title: Binding duty or guidance?
cards.prompt: Sort each statement by where it comes from.

items.text: A bank must have an IT steering committee
A bank must keep cyber resilience
Banks must test the disaster recovery plan at least yearly
Security policy should include a security awareness programme
Default passwords must be changed before systems go live
Phishing simulations at least once a year verify staff awareness
Initial notice of a significant IT incident within 24 hours
Information classes such as secret, internal and public

cards.title: The committee that met without risk
cards.setting: Small meeting room, Jakarta head office. Tuesday, 10:00 am.

lines.text: The steering committee approved moving our card switch to a new vendor last month. The risk director was travelling, so the IT director chaired with the IT head and two business heads.
POJK 11 names the minimum members: the director over IT, the director over risk management, the head of the IT unit and the head of the IT user unit.
So a recommendation without the risk director's view is weak, and the minutes will show it. Directors must also see that IT risk management actually works.
The vendor contract is signed already. Do we tear it up?
Not so fast. Let's decide what to do now.

cards.title: Fixing a flawed approval
cards.situation: The IT steering committee recommended a new card-switch vendor without the director over risk management. The contract is signed and migration starts in six weeks. As the cyber analyst preparing the governance self-check, what do you recommend?

choices.text: Record the gap, take the decision back to a properly constituted committee with a risk and security assessment of the vendor before migration, and report the result to the directors.
choices.outcome: Best. POJK 11 sets the committee's minimum membership and expects risk management in every stage of IT. Re-running the decision with risk input before migration fixes the weakness while there is still time.

choices.text: Leave it: the IT director chaired the meeting, so the committee was properly led.
choices.outcome: Weak. The chair is fine, but a required member was missing and no risk view was given. The self-check would hide a real governance gap.

choices.text: Ask the risk director to sign the minutes afterwards so the file looks complete.
choices.outcome: Poor. Back-filled approval does not create a real risk assessment and misleads the board and OJK examiners.

choices.text: Raise it in next year's IT strategic plan as a lesson learned.
choices.outcome: Partly right. Lessons belong in planning, but waiting a year lets an unassessed vendor go live in six weeks.

cards.back: Peraturan OJK: a binding regulation issued by OJK's Board of Commissioners.
Peraturan Anggota Dewan Komisioner: a regulation issued by an OJK board member to implement a POJK.
Surat Edaran OJK: an OJK circular giving implementing detail.
Pihak penyedia jasa TI: an IT service provider used by the bank.
Disaster recovery plan: how the bank restores data, hardware and software for critical operations.
Data centre and disaster recovery centre; by default both must be in Indonesia.

cards.title: Data location: default and exception
cards.caption: Articles 35-41 of POJK 11/2022. Transaction processing also stays in Indonesia unless OJK permits otherwise.

items.label: Where systems sit
items.left: Data centre and DR centre in Indonesia

items.label: Who decides
items.right: OJK, within three months of a complete application

items.label: Typical cases
items.right: Group risk, AML or internal management systems

items.label: After approval
items.right: Must implement within six months or the permit lapses

cards.question: A bank was warned in writing for lacking an IT steering committee and still has none. What can OJK impose next under POJK 11/2022?
options: A criminal fine on each director personally
Immediate revocation of the bank's licence
A ban on new products, a freeze on some activities and/or a lower governance score
Only a second written warning
cards.explanation: Article 9(2) lets OJK escalate after an unheeded written warning to a ban on issuing new products, a freeze on certain activities and/or a lower governance factor in the soundness rating. Licence revocation and criminal fines are not the sanctions this article provides.

cards.title: Real case: OJK's Digital Resilience Guide (2024)
cards.body:
On **20 August 2024** OJK launched a **Digital Resilience Guide** (Panduan Resiliensi Digital) for commercial banks (press release SP 124/GKPB/OJK/VIII/2024).

OJK said the guide rests on three aspects:

- **Digital competitiveness**: customer-focused products, responsible adoption of new technology, digital leadership, culture and talent.
- **Business continuity management** in three phases: **anticipate**, **withstand and recover**, and **sustain**.
- **Customer care** during disruption: customer incident management, recovery and post-recovery services.

OJK presented it as a reference that complements POJK 11/2022, SEOJK 29/2022 and the 2023 circular on digital maturity assessment, so banks can prepare for, face and recover from technology disruption or cyber incidents while limiting customer loss, reputational damage and financial loss.

**Lesson:** OJK treats IT and cyber resilience as one system: governance, people, continuity and customers together.

cards.title: Read the rule stack in the right order
cards.body: When a question comes up, start with the **POJK 11** article to find the duty and the sanction, then open **PADK 1/2026** or **SEOJK 29/2022** for how to meet it, then your **bank's policy** for who does what. Keep the official Indonesian texts as the reference: OJK publishes them on www.ojk.go.id.

cards.title: Stage one take-aways
items: POJK 11/2022 sets binding IT duties for every commercial bank; it took effect three months after its July 2022 promulgation.
PADK 1/2026 (in force 1 March 2026) gives the detailed IT guide and revoked SEOJK 21/2017; SEOJK 29/2022 covers cyber resilience.
Directors set IT strategy and policy; commissioners oversee; a director chairs the IT steering committee with the IT and risk directors on it.
Breaches start with a written warning and can escalate to a ban on new products, frozen activities or a lower governance score.
Data centres and transaction processing stay in Indonesia unless OJK grants permission.

cards.prompt: Think of one IT decision in your unit this year. Who recommended it, who approved it, and was risk management really part of it? What would you change next time?

quiz.question: Which OJK regulation sets the binding duties on IT governance, cyber resilience and IT incident reporting for commercial banks?
options: POJK 22 of 2023
POJK 11/POJK.03/2022
SEOJK 21/SEOJK.03/2017
POJK 8 of 2023
quiz.explanation: POJK 11/2022 is the regulation on the use of IT by commercial banks. SEOJK 21/2017 was an older circular, revoked by PADK 1/2026; POJK 22/2023 covers consumer protection.

quiz.question: When did PADK 1 of 2026 on IT operation by commercial banks take effect?
options: 1 March 2026
23 January 2026
7 July 2022
27 December 2022
quiz.explanation: PADK 1/2026 was set on 23 January 2026 and took effect on 1 March 2026. 7 July 2022 is when POJK 11 was promulgated, and 27 December 2022 is the date of SEOJK 29.

quiz.question: Under POJK 11/2022, who must at least sit on the IT steering committee?
options: The president commissioner, the internal audit head and the IT head
Every director and the head of each branch region
The compliance director, an external auditor and the IT head
The IT director, the risk director and the heads of the IT unit and of the IT user unit
quiz.explanation: Article 7(3) names the director over the IT unit, the director over risk management, the top official of the IT unit and the top official of the IT user unit. Commissioners oversee IT governance but are not listed members.

quiz.question: A bank's IT steering committee is chaired by the head of the IT unit, who is not a director. What is wrong?
options: Nothing, as long as the IT head reports to the board
The chair must be a commissioner, not an officer
POJK 11 requires the committee to be chaired by one of the bank's directors
The chair must be an independent outside expert
quiz.explanation: Article 7(4) says the committee is chaired by one of the bank's directors who is also a member. Commissioners oversee IT governance rather than chair the committee.

quiz.question: By when must a bank submit its IT strategic plan to OJK?
options: Within 15 working days after the end of the reporting year
By the end of November in the year before the plan period starts
By the end of June in the plan's first year
Within 10 working days after the board approves it
quiz.explanation: Article 13(1) of POJK 11 sets the end of November before the plan period begins. The 15-working-day deadline belongs to the report on the current condition of IT operation.

quiz.question: A bank ignores a written warning for failing to keep cyber resilience. Which further sanction is available to OJK under POJK 11/2022?
options: A lower governance factor score in the bank's soundness rating
A criminal prison term for the head of IT
Automatic transfer of the bank to Bank Indonesia's control
A mandatory public apology in national newspapers
quiz.explanation: Article 27(2) allows a ban on new products, a freeze on certain business activities and/or a lower governance factor in the soundness rating. Prison terms are not POJK sanctions.

quiz.question: A regional bank wants to host its core banking system in a data centre in Singapore. What does POJK 11/2022 say?
options: It is allowed if the provider is ISO 27001 certified
It is allowed if customers are told in the terms and conditions
Systems sit in Indonesia; placing them abroad needs OJK permission and must meet set criteria
It is banned outright with no exceptions
quiz.explanation: Article 35 puts data centres and DR centres in Indonesia by default, with offshore placement only by OJK permit for listed kinds of systems such as group risk or AML systems. Certification or customer notice alone does not replace the permit.

quiz.question: Which statement best describes how PADK 1/2026 relates to POJK 11/2022?
options: It replaces POJK 11 entirely from March 2026
It applies only to Sharia business units
It is a voluntary industry code with no legal force
It implements POJK 11 with detailed guidance, report formats and permit procedures
quiz.explanation: PADK 1/2026 was issued to carry out several articles of POJK 11 and sets out a guide, reporting procedures and formats. POJK 11 stays in force; PADK 1 revoked only the old circular SEOJK 21/2017.

quiz.question: POJK 11/2022 says information security must cover four aspects of IT operation. Which list is correct?
options: Human resources, process, technology and the physical or environmental side
Hardware, software, network and data only
Confidentiality, integrity, availability and privacy
Front office, back office, IT and audit
quiz.explanation: Article 16(2) lists human resources, process, technology and physical or environmental aspects. Confidentiality, integrity and availability are the goals of security, not the four aspects.

quiz.question: A director asks why tellers need IT security training when the IT unit runs the systems. Which point from POJK 11 answers best?
options: Tellers are legally IT staff because they use terminals
Good IT governance applies to every IT user unit as well as the IT unit itself
OJK tests every teller personally each year
Only tellers handle customer passwords
quiz.explanation: Article 2(4) applies good IT governance to IT managing units and IT user units. Article 16 adds that security covers people. Tellers are users, which is why they are in scope; OJK does not test individual tellers.

sessions.title: The Human Firewall: Security Policy, People and Access under PADK 1/2026
sessions.summary: Apply PADK 1/2026's people-centred security controls: the security policy and awareness programme, screening, confidentiality, role-based training for staff, consultants, temps and provider staff, access control and incident reporting.
objectives: List what the information security policy must contain, including training and awareness
Identify who must receive security training or briefings and how it is tailored to roles
Apply PADK 1/2026 access, password and information classification rules
Recognise social engineering and report suspected incidents to the point of contact

cards.title: The contractor with the master password
cards.setting: IT operations floor, Bank Lintas Kepulauan data centre, Jakarta. Wednesday, 7:40 am.

lines.text: Bad start. A consultant from our network vendor left three weeks ago, but his administrator account still works. Last night it logged in at 2 am.
Did he sign a confidentiality agreement? Did anyone remove his access when the contract ended?
He signed the vendor's agreement, not ours. And nobody told us his assignment ended. He never did our security briefing either; it was only for employees.
That server holds deposit data. If it was him, or someone using his password, we may have a secrecy problem as well as a security one.
Our branches have temps and outsourced cleaners with badges too. Are they part of this?
Stage two is the Human Firewall. PADK 1/2026 puts people at the centre of information security: employees, consultants, temporary staff and provider staff. Let's see what it expects.

scenes.heading: Everyone with access
scenes.narration: PADK 1/2026 says employees, consultants, temporary staff and IT provider staff who can reach information must understand their security duties, with roles defined by what access they need.

scenes.heading: Before hiring
scenes.narration: For roles where a breach would do great harm, such as network or system administrators, banks should screen candidates first, for example with criminal-record background checks.

scenes.heading: Written promises
scenes.narration: Employment contracts carry security and confidentiality clauses. Provider contracts include non-disclosure terms, and provider staff working at the bank with data access sign their own confidentiality agreement.

scenes.heading: Training by role
scenes.narration: Training or briefings on information security must reach employees, consultants, temporary staff and provider staff, tailored to each person's role and responsibilities.

scenes.heading: On the way out
scenes.narration: When a role changes or a contract ends, assets come back and access rights are changed or closed. Breaking the security policy carries sanctions the bank sets.

cards.title: The people-security life cycle
cards.caption: Drawn from PADK 1/2026, information security procedures for human resources.

items.label: Screen
items.detail: Background checks for high-impact roles before hiring or onboarding.

items.label: Commit
items.detail: Contracts and NDAs with confidentiality and security clauses.

items.label: Train
items.detail: Role-based training or briefings for staff, consultants, temps and provider staff.

items.label: Monitor
items.detail: Access reviews, logs and reporting of incidents to the point of contact.

items.label: Exit
items.detail: Return assets and change or close access when duties change or end.

cards.title: In scope for security training?
cards.prompt: PADK 1/2026 lists who must receive information security training or briefings. Sort these people.

items.text: A permanent teller in Makassar
A temporary staff member in the call centre
An outsourced developer from the IT provider working on the core system
A consultant reviewing the network design
A customer using the mobile app
A shareholder attending the annual meeting
A system administrator on a fixed-term contract
A journalist visiting the head office lobby

cards.question: Under PADK 1/2026, who must receive information security training or briefings?
options: Employees, consultants, temporary staff and IT provider staff, according to their roles
Only permanent employees in the IT unit
Only staff who handle customer deposits
Directors and commissioners only, who then cascade it
cards.explanation: PADK 1/2026 says training and/or briefings on information security are given to bank employees, consultants, temporary staff and IT provider staff, matched to their roles and responsibilities. Limiting it to IT or deposit staff leaves gaps that attackers use.

cards.title: What the security policy must contain
Classify before you protect
cards.caption: PADK 1/2026 gives secret, internal and public as example classes; the bank sets its own scheme.

items.label: Secret
items.left: Customer deposit data, customer personal data

items.label: Internal
items.left: Internal rules such as staff salary regulations

items.label: Public
items.left: Product information offered to the public

items.label: How to set classes
items.left: By value, confidentiality, legal rules and importance

cards.back: Something you know (PIN, password), something you have (phone, chip card, token), something you are (biometrics), chosen by risk.
Access is granted on business need and kept to the minimum.
Unique, random, delivered securely and changed at first login.
Default passwords and user-IDs on systems and devices are changed before go-live.
Long enough, at least two character types, not based on personal data, not common words, changed periodically, not reused.
Lock after a set number of failed logins, disable idle IDs, and have a unit outside access operations review rights regularly.

cards.title: A call to the branch
cards.setting: Bank Lintas Kepulauan branch, Makassar. Thursday, 4:50 pm.

lines.text: A caller says he's from head office IT. Our branch system shows an error, he says, and he needs the supervisor's user-ID and the code from her token to fix it before end-of-day.
He knows our branch code and the supervisor's name. He sounds calm and senior. The supervisor is about to read the code out.
This is a classic impersonation call. SEOJK 29 lists scam phone and impersonation calls among the threats staff should be trained to recognise.
What should she do right now?

cards.title: The voice from 'head office'
cards.situation: A caller claiming to be head office IT asks a branch supervisor for her user-ID and current token code to fix an error before end-of-day. He knows internal names and codes. What should the supervisor do?

choices.text: Refuse to share any credential, end the call, verify through the bank's official IT service desk number, and report the call to the security incident point of contact.
choices.outcome: Best. Users must keep passwords and PINs secret, and PADK 1/2026 expects staff to report any sign of a security incident to the designated point of contact so the bank can warn other branches.

choices.text: Give the user-ID but not the token code, since IDs are not secret.
choices.outcome: Partly wrong. The user-ID helps the attacker and the call itself is an incident that should be reported. Verify independently instead.

choices.text: Read out both, then change the password tomorrow.
choices.outcome: Poor. A token code can be used at once; changing the password later does not undo a fraudulent session tonight.

choices.text: Ask the caller security questions about the branch before sharing.
choices.outcome: Poor. Attackers often know internal details already. Verification must use a channel the bank controls, not the caller's answers.

cards.title: Reporting a suspected security incident
cards.prompt: Put the steps PADK 1/2026 describes for a reported security incident in order.
steps: A staff member, temp or provider employee spots a sign of a possible security incident
They report it to the designated point of contact through the set reporting channel
The point of contact verifies the report against what the system shows
The point of contact assesses whether it is a security incident and passes it to the response team
The response team handles it under its playbook and reports to management

cards.question: Which password practice is in line with PADK 1/2026?
options: Writing the password on paper kept in the desk drawer
Using at least two character types and avoiding names, phone numbers and birth dates
Reusing a strong password across all systems
Keeping the vendor's default administrator password
cards.explanation: PADK 1/2026 asks users to pick passwords long enough, with at least two types of characters, not based on personal data, and not common words; to keep them secret and not reuse them; and banks must change default passwords before go-live.

cards.title: Real case: the Indonesia Anti-Scam Centre's first 14 months
cards.body:
On **21 January 2026** OJK reported (press release SP 15/GKPB/OJK/I/2026) that the **Indonesia Anti-Scam Centre (IASC)** had returned about **IDR 161 billion** to **1,070** scam victims, from funds blocked at **14 banks** used by fraudsters, counting from the centre's start on 22 November 2024 to 12 January 2026.

OJK named the common methods: shopping fraud, **impersonation and fake calls**, investment and job scams, social-media fraud and love scams. It listed the hard parts: surging complaints, slow reporting, the need for faster blocking and complex flight of funds. OJK stressed that the faster a report is made, the more money can be recovered.

**Lesson for staff:** the same tricks that fool customers are aimed at bank staff. Speed of reporting matters inside the bank too.

cards.title: Make the human controls real
cards.body:
- Put **security clauses** in every employment contract and **NDAs** for every provider employee with data access.
- Link HR leaver and transfer lists to **access removal** the same day, including vendor staff.
- Give **role-based** sessions: tellers on impersonation, admins on privileged access, developers on secure coding.
- Publish one **point of contact** for suspected incidents and thank people who report.

cards.title: Stage two take-aways
items: The security policy must include training and a security awareness programme, roles, and sanctions for breaches.
Training or briefings reach employees, consultants, temporary staff and IT provider staff, tailored to roles.
High-impact IT roles need pre-hire checks; contracts and NDAs bind staff and provider employees to confidentiality.
Access follows least privilege, strong authentication, changed defaults, lockout and independent periodic review.
Anyone who sees a sign of a security incident reports it to the bank's point of contact.

cards.prompt: Who in your team is not a permanent employee but can reach bank information? When did they last receive a security briefing, and who removes their access when they leave?

quiz.question: PADK 1/2026 lists the minimum contents of a bank's information security policy. Which item is on that list?
options: Training and a programme to raise information security awareness
The brand of firewall the bank must buy
The names of all employees with system access
A guarantee that no incident will ever occur
quiz.explanation: The policy must include training and a security awareness programme, along with objectives, commitment, a control framework, compliance, roles, sanctions and supporting documents. Product brands and staff lists belong in standards or records, not the policy.

quiz.question: A vendor's engineer works on site with access to bank data. Under PADK 1/2026, what should be in place besides the bank-vendor contract?
options: Nothing more, because the contract binds the vendor's staff
A deposit paid by the engineer as security
The engineer's own signed confidentiality agreement and a role-based security briefing
Approval from OJK for each vendor engineer
quiz.explanation: PADK 1/2026 asks for NDA clauses in the provider contract and for every provider employee assigned to the bank with data access to sign a confidentiality agreement; provider staff also receive security training or briefings by role.

quiz.question: For which role does PADK 1/2026 give background checks as an example of pre-hire control?
options: Branch customer service officer
Marketing executive
Office receptionist
Network or system administrator
quiz.explanation: PADK 1/2026 gives criminal-record and data-theft background checks for network or system administrator posts, as roles with great impact on information security.

quiz.question: A consultant's contract ends on 31 May, but HR only learns of it in July. What control did the bank miss?
options: An annual penetration test of the consultant's laptop
A procedure to return assets and change or close access when duties or contracts end
A disaster recovery test including the consultant
A data protection impact assessment
quiz.explanation: PADK 1/2026 requires procedures to return assets and change or close access for employees, consultants, temporary staff and provider staff when duties change or contracts end. The other tests do not address leaver access.

quiz.question: Which example classification does PADK 1/2026 give for customer deposit data?
options: Secret
Internal
Public
Restricted to IT only
quiz.explanation: PADK 1/2026 gives 'secret' (rahasia) as the class for customer deposit data and customer personal data, 'internal' for things like staff salary rules, and 'public' for product information.

quiz.question: Which authentication approach fits PADK 1/2026 for a high-risk administrator console?
options: Use a shared team password so nobody gets locked out
Rely on the network firewall and skip user authentication
Combine factors chosen by risk analysis, such as a password plus a hardware token
Use the device's default administrator account
quiz.explanation: PADK 1/2026 asks banks to choose identification and authentication methods by risk, using one or a combination of what you know, what you have and what you are. Shared and default accounts break accountability and default credentials must be changed.

quiz.question: Who should review user access rights periodically under PADK 1/2026?
options: The users themselves through self-certification
The vendor who installed the system
OJK supervisors during each visit
A unit that is not involved in operating access control
quiz.explanation: PADK 1/2026 asks for periodic reviews of access rights by a unit not involved in access control operations, so rights match the authority given. Self-certification lacks independence.

quiz.question: A teller receives a call from 'head office IT' asking for her token code. She refuses and hangs up. What else should she do?
options: Nothing, because no harm was done
Report the call to the bank's security incident point of contact
Call the number the caller gave to confirm
Post a warning on her personal social media
quiz.explanation: PADK 1/2026 expects employees to report any sign or potential of a security incident to the designated point of contact. Calling back a number the caller supplied may reach the fraudster.

quiz.question: Which statement about the security policy matches PADK 1/2026?
options: It is communicated regularly to all personnel and relevant external parties
It is a confidential board document shown only to the IT head
It is written once and never changed
It is the same for every bank and issued by OJK
quiz.explanation: PADK 1/2026 says the policy must suit the bank's risk appetite, be communicated regularly to all personnel and relevant outside parties, and be evaluated regularly and after important changes.

quiz.question: A bank trains permanent staff on security every year but excludes the IT service provider's helpdesk engineers working at the bank, because they are the vendor's employees. Assess this under PADK 1/2026.
options: It is fine, because the vendor carries the risk
It is fine if the vendor holds an ISO certificate
It falls short only if the engineers handle cash
It falls short: provider staff must also receive security training or briefings suited to their role
quiz.explanation: PADK 1/2026 names IT provider staff, consultants and temporary staff alongside employees for security training or briefings. A certificate or contract does not move the bank's duty to the vendor.

sessions.title: Cyber Resilience under SEOJK 29/2022: Ratings, Testing and Awareness
sessions.summary: Work through the four cyber resilience processes, the yearly inherent risk and maturity ratings, vulnerability and scenario testing, the independent cyber unit and the yearly awareness programme with phishing simulation.
objectives: Explain the four cyber resilience processes required by POJK 11 Article 21
Describe the yearly cyber risk and maturity assessments and how they reach OJK
Distinguish vulnerability-based from scenario-based testing and their reporting deadlines
Apply SEOJK 29/2022 expectations on the cyber unit, awareness, phishing simulation and capacity building

cards.title: The phishing test nobody liked
cards.setting: Cyber Resilience and Security Unit, Jakarta. Monday, 9:00 am.

lines.text: Results of last week's phishing simulation are in. We sent a fake parcel-delivery email to every employee.
Medan region: about one in six clicked, and some typed their credentials into the fake page. Two branch heads complained we tricked their staff.
My tellers felt ambushed. Is this test even required, or did the unit invent it?
OJK's cyber circular, SEOJK 29/2022, names phishing simulation to all staff, at least once a year, as one way to check awareness. And it expects an awareness programme at least yearly.
Then the question isn't whether to test. It's what we do with the results, and what else the circular expects of us.
Exactly. Stage three is the Cyber Watchtower: the four cyber resilience processes, risk and maturity ratings, testing, the cyber unit and the awareness programme.

scenes.heading: Identify
scenes.narration: Keep an inventory of IT assets and configurations, find vulnerabilities, follow current cyber threats and test security regularly.

scenes.heading: Protect
scenes.narration: Apply security controls that fit the assets and threats: data security, network and device protection, access control, secure coding, patching, and protection when using providers and cloud.

scenes.heading: Detect
scenes.narration: Know the normal baseline of critical functions, monitor for suspicious activity, keep watching for vulnerabilities and analyse threats behind incidents.

scenes.heading: Respond and recover
scenes.narration: Have a response and recovery plan and team, contain the damage, escalate and report through set channels, and learn lessons after each incident.

scenes.heading: Why it matters
scenes.narration: POJK 11 makes these four processes the minimum for keeping cyber resilience, supported by an adequate information system. SEOJK 29 sets out what each involves.

cards.title: The cyber resilience cycle (POJK 11 Article 21)
cards.caption: SEOJK 29/2022 section IV describes the minimum for each process.

items.label: Identify assets, threats, weaknesses
items.detail: Inventory, vulnerability identification, threat watch, regular testing.

items.label: Protect assets
items.detail: Controls, data security, access, secure coding, patching, provider and cloud safeguards.

items.label: Detect incidents
items.detail: Baselines, monitoring, continuous vulnerability watch, threat analysis.

items.label: Respond and recover
items.detail: Plan, team, containment, escalation, reporting, lessons learned.

cards.title: Match the SEOJK 29 assessment to its scale
cards.prompt: Each yearly cyber assessment uses its own rating scale.

pairs.right: Five ratings from low to high, based on technology, products, organisation and incident record.

pairs.left: Quality of risk management and of resilience processes
pairs.right: Five ratings from Strong to Unsatisfactory.
Combines inherent risk and maturity into five ratings from low to high.

cards.question: For which position date does a bank assess its inherent cyber risk and cyber maturity each year?
options: The end of December
The end of June
The bank's financial year-end, whatever month it is
The date of the last cyber incident
cards.explanation: SEOJK 29/2022 sets both assessments yearly for the end-of-December position, with updates any time if needed. Results go to OJK in the report on the current condition of IT operation within 15 working days after the reporting year ends.

cards.title: Assess, rate and report every year
cards.body:
SEOJK 29/2022 sets an annual cycle:

- **Inherent risk**: rate cyber risk from four factors: **technology** (for example internet links, third-party connections, cloud use, end-of-life systems, personal devices), **bank products** (online and mobile channels, ATMs, card products), **organisational characteristics** (such as turnover of IT and cyber staff) and **cyber incident track record**.
- **Maturity**: rate the quality of cyber risk management (governance, framework, process and people, controls) and of the four resilience processes.
- **Risk level**: combine inherent risk and maturity.

All are as at **end of December** and go to OJK in the **report on the current condition of IT operation**, within **15 working days** after the reporting year. OJK may adjust ratings that do not reflect reality, and uses them in the **bank soundness** assessment.

cards.title: Two kinds of cyber security testing
cards.caption: POJK 11 Articles 23-25 and SEOJK 29 section VII. A scenario test counts as complete when its report is finished.

items.label: Examples
items.right: Table-top, cyber range, social engineering, attack simulation

items.label: How often
items.left: Regularly, set by criticality and change

items.label: Report to OJK
items.left: In the yearly IT condition report
items.right: Within 10 working days after the test is complete

cards.title: Which kind of test is it?
cards.prompt: Sort each exercise by the kind of cyber security test SEOJK 29/2022 places it in.

items.text: Penetration test of the mobile banking app
Table-top exercise on a ransomware attack with executives
Phishing email sent to all staff to measure awareness
Red team versus blue team attack simulation
Scan of internet-facing servers for known weaknesses
Cyber range exercise on a simulated copy of the network
Penetration test after a major change to the core system

cards.title: Who checks the checkers?
cards.setting: Board corridor, Jakarta head office. Wednesday, 2:00 pm.

lines.text: The IT director wants the cyber unit to report to the head of IT operations. 'Fewer meetings,' he says.
I run IT operations. If the cyber unit reports to me, it audits my patching and my change control. That feels wrong.
POJK 11 Article 26 requires a unit or function for cyber resilience and security that is independent of IT management: planning, building, operating and monitoring IT.
The circular adds that it coordinates the cyber incident response team, which an official of the cyber unit leads.

cards.title: Where should the cyber unit sit?
cards.situation: The IT director proposes moving the cyber resilience and security unit under the head of IT operations to cut meetings. The bank is mid-sized. What do you advise the directors?

choices.text: Keep the unit independent of IT management, with a reporting line that suits the bank's size and leads to the directors; improve coordination through a joint working forum instead.
choices.outcome: Best. POJK 11 Article 26 requires independence from IT management, and the elucidation lets the bank size the unit and its accountability line to the directors. Coordination can improve without losing independence.

choices.text: Accept the move but ask IT operations to sign a declaration of independence.
choices.outcome: Poor. A declaration does not change the fact that the unit would report to the function it must challenge.

choices.text: Merge the unit into internal audit so it is independent of everyone.
choices.outcome: Partly right on independence, but the cyber unit runs and coordinates day-to-day resilience, testing and incident response, which is a management role, not third-line audit.

choices.text: Outsource the whole unit to the IT provider that runs the data centre.
choices.outcome: Poor. The provider is part of what must be assessed, and the bank stays responsible for its cyber unit and its tests.

cards.back: Run regularly and continuously, at least once a year, for example through seminars, discussions, workshops or spreading cyber policies and procedures.
Review and update the programme so it covers the cyber threats that are relevant and emerging.
One method: phishing simulation by email to all employees at least once a year.
A continuing programme for relevant staff, including directors, commissioners and management, matched to each role.
Assess staff cyber knowledge and skills and use the results to plan capacity building.
Build a culture of cyber responsibility for staff at every level and strong commitment to cyber security.

cards.question: According to SEOJK 29/2022, how often should a bank at least run its cyber security awareness programme and its staff phishing simulation?
options: Once at induction and then only after an incident
Every three years, matching the external audit review
Monthly, as a fixed legal minimum for every bank
At least once a year for each
cards.explanation: The circular's assessment criteria expect an awareness programme run regularly and at least once a year, and give phishing simulation to all staff at least once a year as a way to verify understanding. It does not set a monthly minimum.

cards.title: Real case: OJK announces a cyber incident task force (2025)
cards.body:
In its press release on the **June 2025** monthly board meeting, issued on **8 July 2025** (SP 99/GKPB/OJK/VII/2025), OJK said that, facing the **rising risk of cyber incidents** that threaten financial-sector stability, it was **strengthening IT rules for banking** and would form a **task force for handling cyber incidents** so responses are more coordinated, faster and more effective.

OJK also urged every financial services business to **raise cyber resilience** and **strengthen coordination with regulators**. The same release asked banks to monitor dormant accounts, tackle account trading and report suspicious use to PPATK.

PADK 1/2026, issued six months later, followed that signal with a full IT operating guide.

**Lesson:** OJK's message is that resilience is not only a bank's internal matter; fast, coordinated communication with the supervisor is part of it.

cards.title: Make the phishing test a teaching moment
cards.body:
- Announce that simulations happen, but not when.
- Show anyone who clicks a short **learning page** at once, not a reprimand.
- Report results to directors **by unit and trend**, not by name, and feed weak spots into the next awareness cycle.
- Celebrate staff who **report** the fake email: reporting rate matters as much as click rate.
- Cover what SEOJK 29 lists: phishing, scam phone and impersonation calls, safe handling of sensitive data, accidental leaks such as lost phones or misdirected email.

cards.title: Stage three take-aways
items: Cyber resilience means identify, protect, detect, and respond and recover, backed by an adequate information system.
Inherent cyber risk and cyber maturity are rated yearly as at end of December and reported in the IT condition report.
Vulnerability tests run regularly; scenario tests run at least yearly and are reported within 10 working days of completion.
The cyber unit must be independent of IT management and coordinates the cyber incident response team.
Awareness runs at least yearly, phishing simulations verify it, and capacity building reaches staff up to the boards.

cards.prompt: If your bank ran a phishing simulation tomorrow, would you report the email or click it? What would help your colleagues report more often?

quiz.question: Which four processes does POJK 11/2022 Article 21 require a bank to carry out to keep cyber resilience?
options: Identify assets, threats and weaknesses; protect assets; detect incidents; respond and recover
Plan, build, run and monitor IT systems
Prevent, insure, outsource and audit cyber risk
Classify, encrypt, back up and delete data
quiz.explanation: Article 21(2) lists identification of assets, threats and vulnerabilities; protection of assets; detection of cyber incidents; and response and recovery. Plan, build, run and monitor are the activities of IT management under Article 8.

quiz.question: Which factors does SEOJK 29/2022 use to assess inherent cyber risk?
options: Capital, assets, management and earnings
Technology, bank products, organisational characteristics and cyber incident record
Governance, framework, process and controls
Customers, geography, channels and products
quiz.explanation: The circular assesses inherent cyber risk from technology, bank products, organisational characteristics and the cyber incident track record. Governance, framework, process and controls are the aspects of cyber risk management quality used in the maturity assessment.

quiz.question: A bank ran a ransomware table-top exercise on 3 November and finished the report on 14 November. When is the report due to OJK?
options: Within 10 working days after 3 November
Within 24 hours of the exercise
Within 10 working days after 14 November, when the report was completed
With the yearly IT condition report in January
quiz.explanation: SEOJK 29 says a scenario test is treated as complete when its report is finished, and the report goes to OJK within 10 working days after completion. Vulnerability test results, by contrast, go in the yearly IT condition report.

quiz.question: How should results of penetration tests done in March, July and November be submitted to OJK?
options: Each within 10 working days of the test
Each within 24 hours as an incident notice
Only on request during an OJK examination
Compiled in the report on the current condition of IT operation after the year ends
quiz.explanation: Vulnerability-based test results go to OJK as part of the yearly report on the current condition of IT operation, within 15 working days after the reporting year. The 10-working-day rule is for scenario-based tests.

quiz.question: Which kind of exercise does SEOJK 29/2022 describe as using manipulation of less alert staff, for example through phishing and spam, to measure awareness?
options: Social engineering exercise
Cyber range exercise
Penetration test
Business impact analysis
quiz.explanation: The circular lists the social engineering exercise among scenario-based tests and says it can show the level of staff cyber awareness. A cyber range exercise uses a simulated copy of the bank's systems.

quiz.question: What does POJK 11/2022 require about the unit that handles cyber resilience and security?
options: It must be part of the IT operations team
It must be independent of the IT management function
It must be run by an outside provider
It must report directly to OJK rather than the directors
quiz.explanation: Article 26 requires the unit or function to be independent of IT management. The elucidation lets the bank size it and set its accountability line to the directors; it does not report to OJK instead of the bank.

quiz.question: A bank's awareness programme has used the same slides since 2022. Which SEOJK 29 expectation does this miss?
options: Running the programme at least every three years
Translating the slides into English
Reviewing and updating the programme so it covers relevant and emerging cyber threats
Having OJK approve the slides in advance
quiz.explanation: The circular expects the awareness programme to be reviewed regularly and updated so its content matches current and emerging threats. There is no OJK pre-approval or English requirement.

quiz.question: Who leads the cyber incident response team according to SEOJK 29/2022?
options: The head of corporate communications
The external forensic provider
The internal audit head
An official from the cyber resilience and security unit
quiz.explanation: The circular says the cyber unit coordinates the response team and that the team is led by an official from that unit. Communications, legal, HR and providers support it.

quiz.question: Which topics does SEOJK 29/2022 suggest for cyber capacity building of relevant staff?
options: Social engineering such as phishing and impersonation calls, safe handling of sensitive data and accidental data leaks
Only firewall configuration for network engineers
Only the bank's marketing of digital products
Only physical security of branches
quiz.explanation: The listed topics include current threats and social engineering (phishing, scam phone and impersonation calls), attack tactics, secure authentication and handling of sensitive data, accidental leaks, data protection, secure coding and incident response, matched to each role.

quiz.question: A director says the cyber awareness programme is for staff, not the board. Which response reflects SEOJK 29/2022?
options: Directors are exempt if they hold a risk management certificate
Board awareness is optional for banks below a certain size
Capacity building should reach relevant staff including directors, commissioners and management
Only commissioners need it, because they supervise
quiz.explanation: The circular expects a continuing cyber capacity programme for relevant staff including the boards and management, and expects directors and commissioners to understand cyber risk management. No exemption by certificate or size is given.

sessions.title: Incidents, IT Providers and Disaster Recovery: Reporting to OJK
sessions.summary: Report significant IT and cyber incidents to OJK within 24 hours and 5 working days, handle incidents step by step, oversee IT providers and their critical events, and keep a tested disaster recovery plan.
objectives: Decide when an IT or cyber incident must be reported and meet the 24-hour and 5-working-day deadlines
Apply the rule for other authorities with faster or slower deadlines
Follow PADK 1/2026's incident handling steps, including forensically sound evidence
Apply POJK 11 rules on IT provider contracts, 3-working-day reports and disaster recovery testing

cards.title: Saturday night, mobile banking down
cards.setting: Security operations room, Jakarta data centre. Saturday, 11:40 pm.

lines.text: Mobile banking has been down for forty minutes. Traffic from thousands of addresses is flooding the login service. It looks like a DDoS attack.
Customers can't transfer money on a Saturday night and social media is already noisy. This could be a significant cyber incident.
Clock check: when did we know? The monitoring alert fired at 11:02 pm and Made confirmed the attack at 11:15.
Our payment switch provider also says one of its servers was hit. Their contract says they must tell us about critical events.
Do we fix it first and report on Monday? Monday is a working day.
No. Stage four is the Alarm Room: OJK's incident reporting clock, the response steps, providers and disaster recovery. The clock is already running.

scenes.heading: What counts
scenes.narration: An IT incident is a critical event, misuse or crime in IT operation. It is either a cyber incident, such as malware, ransomware, web defacement or denial of service, or a non-cyber incident.

scenes.heading: When to report
scenes.narration: Reporting is required when an incident has caused, or could cause, significant loss or disruption to operations. Loss can be financial or non-financial, such as negative news that hurts reputation.

scenes.heading: Twenty-four hours
scenes.narration: The bank sends an initial notice within 24 hours after it becomes aware of the incident, in writing by electronic means such as official email, to its OJK supervisors, using the information available.

scenes.heading: Five working days
scenes.narration: A fuller incident report follows online through OJK's reporting system within five working days after the bank became aware of the incident.

scenes.heading: When another authority is faster
scenes.narration: If another authority requires faster notice or reporting, the bank sends the same notice or report to OJK at the same time it meets that faster deadline.

cards.title: From alert to OJK report
cards.caption: POJK 11/2022 Article 60, SEOJK 29/2022 section IX (cyber) and PADK 1/2026 (non-cyber).

items.label: Alert fires
items.detail: Monitoring flags unusual traffic; staff verify and escalate.

items.label: Bank becomes aware
items.detail: The reporting clock starts when the bank knows of the incident.

items.label: Initial notice
items.detail: Written electronic notice to the bank's OJK supervisors with initial facts.

items.label: Incident report
items.detail: Fuller report online via OJK's reporting system.

items.label: Lessons learned
items.detail: Post-incident analysis updates plans and playbooks.

cards.question: A cyber incident with significant impact becomes known to a bank at 11:15 pm on Saturday. By when is the initial notice to OJK due?
options: By the end of Monday, the next working day
Within five working days
Within 24 hours, so by 11:15 pm on Sunday
Only after the incident has been resolved
cards.explanation: The initial notice is due within 24 hours after the bank becomes aware of the incident, regardless of weekends. The five-working-day limit is for the fuller incident report.

cards.title: Two incident tracks, one discipline
cards.body:
Since **1 March 2026**, PADK 1/2026 sets the reporting procedure and formats for **non-cyber** IT incidents, such as a failed system upgrade or a data centre power failure. **Cyber** incidents follow **SEOJK 29/2022** and its formats. The deadlines are the same:

- **Initial notice** within **24 hours** after the bank is aware, written and electronic, to its OJK supervisors, with the initial information available. The bank makes sure OJK actually received it.
- **Incident report** within **5 working days**, online through OJK's reporting system, with fuller analysis and handling.

If another authority's rules demand faster notice, the bank sends to OJK **at the same time**; if they are slower, OJK's deadlines still apply.

A **late initial notice** draws a written warning under POJK 11 Article 63, then heavier sanctions if not corrected. An **incomplete** report is sanctioned under OJK's reporting rules.

cards.title: Handling a security incident (PADK 1/2026)
cards.prompt: Put the response team's steps in order.
steps: Document all information about the incident
Collect and preserve evidence with forensically sound methods
Apply the fix after management approval, escalating to crisis procedures if it cannot be contained
Write a full report to management and update the playbook with lessons learned

cards.title: Which deadline applies?
cards.prompt: Sort each task by the time limit set in POJK 11/2022 or the related OJK rules.

items.text: Initial notice of a significant ransomware attack
Full cyber incident report through OJK's reporting system
Reporting to OJK that an IT provider breached bank secrecy rules
Initial notice of a significant data centre power failure
Full report on a non-cyber IT incident
Reporting to OJK that the bank ended an IT provider contract early
Reporting to OJK that a key IT provider is going insolvent

cards.title: The provider's bad news
cards.setting: Video call with the payment switch provider. Sunday, 9:00 am.

lines.text: The provider confirms attackers reached a server holding a file of our customers' names and account numbers. They found it four days ago and told us only now.
Four days! Our contract requires them to report critical events to us. And customer data means bank secrecy and personal data are in play.
POJK 11 Article 32 lists situations where the bank must act: one is a provider breaching the rules on bank secrecy or customers' personal data.
So we have our own incident clock and a provider clock. What goes to OJK first?

cards.title: A provider breach on top of an attack
cards.situation: Your payment switch provider admits attackers reached a server with customer names and account numbers four days ago and told the bank only today. The bank is also handling a DDoS attack. What is the right course?

choices.text: Treat it as a significant incident: send OJK the initial notice within 24 hours of the bank learning of it, report the provider condition to OJK within 3 working days, decide follow-up including possible termination, and enforce the contract's reporting clause.
choices.outcome: Best. The bank's 24-hour clock runs from when the bank knew, the provider breach is a listed condition requiring a report within 3 working days under Article 32, and the bank must decide its response.

choices.text: Wait for the provider's own forensic report before telling OJK anything.
choices.outcome: Poor. The initial notice is based on the information available; waiting breaks the 24-hour limit and leaves supervisors blind.

choices.text: Report only the DDoS attack, because the data was on the provider's server, not the bank's.
choices.outcome: Poor. Using a provider does not move the bank's responsibility; the bank must supervise outsourced IT and report the provider condition.

choices.text: Terminate the contract at once and report later in the annual IT condition report.
choices.outcome: Partly right on taking action, but abrupt exit without a plan risks disruption, and the reporting deadlines are days, not a year.

cards.title: Disaster recovery planning (POJK 11 Art. 18, PADK 1/2026)
cards.caption: PADK 1/2026: place the DR centre so its risk exposure differs from that of the main data centre.

items.label: Business impact analysis
items.detail: Rank critical processes; set tolerable downtime (MTD), recovery time (RTO) and data loss (RPO).

items.label: Risk assessment
items.detail: Likelihood and severity of disruptions; gap analysis.

items.label: Recovery strategies
items.detail: Options for minor, major and catastrophic events.

items.label: Procedures
items.detail: Emergency response, system recovery, data synchronisation.

items.label: Tested plan
items.detail: Tested at least yearly on all critical systems with IT users; reviewed yearly.

cards.back: A bank using IT providers must be able to supervise the activities they run for it.

Staff competence, confidentiality of bank and customer data, periodic independent IT audit results, approval of subcontracting, reporting of critical events, termination, and OJK access for examination.
Monitor reliability, independent audit evidence of controls, and service levels against the SLA.
Conditions such as provider insolvency, serious performance decline, or a breach of bank secrecy or customer personal data rules.
Before ending a provider, prepare an exit plan, test continuity and make sure operations are not disrupted.

cards.question: When does a bank have to test its disaster recovery plan under POJK 11/2022?
options: Only when it changes its data centre provider
At least once a year for all critical applications and infrastructure, involving IT users
Every three years with an external auditor
Only after OJK requests it
cards.explanation: Article 18(3) requires a test at least once a year on all critical applications and infrastructure identified by the business impact analysis, involving IT users; Article 18(4) requires a yearly review of the plan.

cards.title: Make the 24-hour notice easy
cards.body:
- Keep the **OJK notice template** and the supervisors' official email addresses in the incident playbook, with a named sender and a backup.
- Log the exact time the bank **became aware** of the incident: that is when the clock starts.
- Send what you know; say what you do not know yet; promise the full report.
- Confirm OJK **received** the notice.
- Check whether another authority has a **faster** deadline and send both at the same time.

cards.title: Real case: OJK and BSSN agree on cyber cooperation (2025)
cards.body:
On **28 November 2025** OJK signed cooperation agreements with the **National Cyber and Crypto Agency (Badan Siber dan Sandi Negara, BSSN)** and with **PPATK**, Indonesia's financial intelligence unit (press release SP 204/GKPB/OJK/XI/2025).

The OJK-BSSN agreements cover strengthening **cyber security and encryption** and building **cyber security capacity**, focused on financial technology innovation and digital financial assets including crypto. They follow a memorandum of understanding signed on 28 February 2024.

OJK's chair, Mahendra Siregar, called cyber attacks a major threat to the security of financial-sector data because they can **erode public trust**, which he described as the greatest risk for the sector.

**Lesson:** incident response is a team sport across the bank, its providers and the authorities. Clear channels before an incident make the 24-hour notice possible.

cards.title: Stage four take-aways
items: Significant IT incidents, cyber or non-cyber, need an initial notice within 24 hours of awareness and a full report within 5 working days.
Cyber incidents follow SEOJK 29/2022; non-cyber incidents follow PADK 1/2026; a faster deadline from another authority applies to OJK at the same time.
Late initial notices are sanctioned, starting with a written warning.
Providers must report critical events to the bank; listed provider problems go to OJK within 3 working days.
The disaster recovery plan rests on a business impact analysis and is tested and reviewed at least yearly.

cards.prompt: If an incident hit your unit at midnight on a public holiday, who would you call first, and does that person know how to start the 24-hour notice to OJK?

quiz.question: How does POJK 11/2022 define an IT incident?
options: Any IT problem a customer complains about
Only an attack by an outside hacker
Any system downtime longer than one hour
A critical event, misuse or crime in IT operation, either cyber or non-cyber
quiz.explanation: The elucidation of Article 60 defines an IT incident as a critical event, misuse and/or crime in IT operation, split into cyber and non-cyber incidents. Reporting duties then depend on significant loss or disruption.

quiz.question: Which incident triggers the reporting duty in POJK 11 Article 60?
options: One that has caused or could cause significant loss or disrupt the bank's operations
Every blocked malware email
Only incidents that cause a financial loss above a fixed rupiah amount
Only incidents already reported in the media
quiz.explanation: Article 60 applies to IT incidents that have caused or may cause significant loss and/or disrupt operations. Loss includes non-financial loss such as negative news; no fixed rupiah threshold is set.

quiz.question: Where does a bank send the initial notice of a significant cyber incident?
options: To the national police cyber unit only
To its OJK supervisors, in writing by electronic means such as official email
To customers through a press release
To Bank Indonesia, which forwards it to OJK
quiz.explanation: POJK 11 and SEOJK 29 direct the initial notice to the bank's supervising unit at OJK, in writing through electronic means; the elucidation gives official email as an example.

quiz.question: Another authority requires a bank to give initial notice of a cyber incident within one hour. The bank notifies that authority after 45 minutes. When should OJK receive its notice?
options: Within 24 hours, as POJK 11 normally allows
Within five working days with the full report
At the same time as the other authority's notice
Only if the other authority asks the bank to inform OJK
quiz.explanation: Where another authority sets a faster deadline, the bank sends the notice or report to OJK at the same time it meets that faster deadline, and is then treated as compliant. Where another authority is slower, OJK's own deadlines apply.

quiz.question: Since PADK 1/2026 took effect, which rules set the reporting format for a non-cyber IT incident such as a failed core system upgrade?
options: PADK 1/2026
SEOJK 29/2022
SEOJK 21/2017
The bank's own template, with no OJK format
quiz.explanation: PADK 1/2026 says its incident reporting provisions apply to non-cyber incidents, while cyber incidents follow the cyber circular, SEOJK 29/2022. SEOJK 21/2017 was revoked.

quiz.question: A bank sends its initial incident notice to OJK three days late. What sanction does POJK 11/2022 provide first?
options: Licence revocation
A ban on all digital channels
An automatic fine per hour of delay
A written warning
quiz.explanation: Article 63 imposes a written warning for a late initial notice, with heavier sanctions (ban on new products, freeze of some activities, lower governance score) if the bank still does not comply.

quiz.question: An IT provider tells the bank it is about to be declared bankrupt. What must the bank do under POJK 11/2022?
options: Wait until the court ruling before acting
Report to OJK within 3 working days of knowing and decide follow-up, including ending the arrangement if needed
Report it in the next yearly IT condition report
Ask OJK to appoint a replacement provider
quiz.explanation: Article 32 lists provider insolvency, liquidation or bankruptcy among conditions requiring action: report to OJK within 3 working days, decide follow-up, and report within 3 working days if the contract is ended early.

quiz.question: Which clause must a bank's contract with an IT provider address under POJK 11 Article 30?
options: A promise that the provider will never subcontract any work
A fixed price for the whole contract term
The provider's willingness to give OJK access to examine the services it provides
A ban on the provider serving other banks
quiz.explanation: The contract must cover, among others, staff competence, confidentiality, independent audit results, bank approval of subcontracting, reporting of critical events, termination, legal compliance and access for OJK. Subcontracting is allowed with the bank's written approval.

quiz.question: What does the business impact analysis in a disaster recovery plan determine, according to PADK 1/2026?
options: The bank's yearly IT budget
The order in which staff take annual leave
Which customers receive compensation first
Criticality of processes and limits such as maximum tolerable downtime, recovery time and recovery point
quiz.explanation: PADK 1/2026 lists the analysis of process criticality, dependencies, provider reliance, MTD, RTO and RPO, minimum resources, communication paths and legal impacts such as customer data confidentiality.

quiz.question: During a DDoS attack, the team wants to restore service by switching to an untested backup route without telling management. What does PADK 1/2026 expect?
options: Solutions are applied after management approval, with escalation to crisis procedures if the incident cannot be contained
The team may act alone because speed is all that matters
The team must first obtain OJK's written approval
The team should wait for the provider to fix it
quiz.explanation: PADK 1/2026 says the response team implements solutions with prior management approval and escalates to management to activate crisis handling if the incident cannot be controlled. OJK approval is not needed for operational fixes.

sessions.title: Bank Secrecy, Personal Data and Readiness for OJK Review
sessions.summary: Protect depositor secrecy under the amended Banking Law, process personal data with proper consent and impact assessments, and keep the audits, reports and training records that show OJK the programme works.
objectives: Apply bank secrecy, its listed exceptions and the penalties for deliberate disclosure
Use PADK 1/2026 rules on consent, impact assessments and data exchange
Meet POJK 11 duties on internal control, audit trails, IT internal audit and external review
Plan the IT reporting calendar and the training evidence an OJK examiner will expect

cards.title: The analytics idea and the examiner's letter
cards.setting: Compliance floor, Jakarta head office. Monday, 8:30 am.

lines.text: Two things this morning. Marketing wants to track customers' locations through the app to offer nearby merchant deals. And OJK has scheduled an IT examination next quarter.
The examiners will ask for our training records, audit results, test reports and incident files. Are they all in one place?
And a lawyer phoned my branch asking for a depositor's balance for a family dispute. My teller nearly read it out.
Location tracking sounds like a data protection question, the lawyer sounds like a secrecy question, and the examination is a question about everything.
Final stage: the Vault and the Review. Bank secrecy, personal data in bank IT, then the audit, reporting and training programme that proves to OJK we do what we say.

scenes.heading: Bank secrecy
scenes.narration: Under the Banking Law, as amended by the P2SK Law of 2023, banks and their affiliated parties must keep information about depositors and their deposits secret.

scenes.heading: Listed exceptions
scenes.narration: Secrecy gives way only in cases the law lists, such as court cases, a depositor's written request or consent, heirs, tax rules, Bank Indonesia's and the deposit insurer's tasks, and treaty cooperation.

scenes.heading: Penalties
scenes.narration: A director, commissioner, employee or other affiliated party who deliberately discloses protected depositor information faces two to four years in prison and a fine of four to eight billion rupiah.

scenes.heading: Personal data
scenes.narration: POJK 11 requires banks to apply personal data protection principles when processing personal data, as set by the personal data protection law, Law 27 of 2022.

scenes.heading: Higher-risk processing
scenes.narration: Where processing could raise risk for customers, such as new technology or tracking location and behaviour, the bank must first assess the impact.

cards.title: Bank secrecy and personal data protection

items.label: Main source
items.left: Banking Law Arts. 40-40C and 47, as amended by P2SK

items.label: What it protects
items.right: Personal data of customers and prospects

items.label: Who must comply
items.left: Banks and affiliated parties; anyone who receives the information
items.right: The bank in all processing, including via third parties

items.left: Listed exceptions; OJK permits for criminal cases

items.label: Breach risk
items.right: OJK sanctions; duties under the data protection law

cards.title: Can the bank disclose depositor information?
cards.prompt: Sort each request by whether the amended Banking Law lists it as an exception to secrecy.

items.text: The depositor's own written request or consent
The lawful heirs of a deceased depositor
Bank Indonesia carrying out monetary, macroprudential or payment-system tasks
Financial information requested under tax law
A lawyer phoning about a family dispute with no court process
A marketing partner wanting balances to target offers
A journalist asking about a celebrity's account
Police in a criminal case, with OJK's permit

cards.question: Who may give permission to open bank secrecy for a criminal court case under the amended Banking Law?
options: OJK
The bank's president director
The depositor's employer
Any police officer without further permission
cards.explanation: Article 40B, inserted by the P2SK Law, gives OJK power to permit opening bank secrecy for criminal cases and for mutual legal assistance; Article 42 sets the written request process for police, prosecutors and judges.

cards.title: Personal data in bank IT: what PADK 1/2026 adds
cards.body:
POJK 11 Articles 43-45 require **effective data management**, **personal data protection principles**, an **impact assessment** where risk rises, and set rules for **data exchange**. PADK 1/2026 gives the detail:

- **Consent** before processing customers' personal data: explicit and documented; **no pre-ticked boxes**; plain language; purpose stated; **separate choices** for different purposes; legal basis explained; customers told they can **withdraw** or **refuse**; consent to unrelated uses is not a condition of service; data deleted after retention ends.
- **Impact assessment** when risk rises, for example **new technology**, **tracking location and behaviour**, **large-scale monitoring of public places**, or **sensitive data on ethnicity, religion, race or inter-group relations**. It describes the processing, tests necessity and proportionality, assesses risks to customers' rights and sets safeguards.
- **Data exchange** rules: policies, agreements (scope, purpose, data types, roles, security, emergencies) and data classes.
- The bank **may appoint an officer** responsible for applying data protection principles.

pairs.right: Personal data protection impact assessment before launch

pairs.right: Redesign consent: explicit, separate per purpose, no pre-ticked boxes

pairs.left: Sharing transaction data with a fintech partner
pairs.right: Data-exchange agreement covering scope, purpose, roles and security

pairs.left: Records kept after the retention period ends
pairs.right: Delete under the data protection rules
