cards.title: Getting ready for the examiners
cards.setting: Cyber unit war room, Jakarta. Thursday, 5:00 pm.

lines.text: Here's what we found. The IT internal audit last ran 18 months ago. The external review of the IT audit function was done four years ago.
And our audit logs on the payment server roll over after 30 days, so we can't trace anything older.
Training records are split: HR has employees, procurement has vendor staff attendance on paper, temps aren't recorded at all.
Then we have a plan to make. Let's decide what to fix first.

cards.title: Fixing the evidence gaps before the examination
cards.situation: With one quarter until OJK's IT examination, the bank finds: no IT internal audit for 18 months, an external review of the IT audit function four years old, short audit-log retention, and scattered training records. What do you recommend?

choices.text: Schedule the yearly IT internal audit now, commission the overdue independent external review, fix log retention to support investigations, and build one training register covering employees, consultants, temps and provider staff; disclose the gaps honestly.
choices.outcome: Best. POJK 11 requires IT internal audit at least yearly, an independent external review of that function at least every three years, and audit trails for supervision and investigation; a single register proves role-based training reached everyone PADK 1/2026 names.

choices.text: Focus on making the training slides look professional; examiners mostly read policies.
choices.outcome: Poor. Examiners test whether controls work: audits, logs and records matter more than slide design.

choices.text: Back-date the internal audit report to last year so the cycle looks unbroken.
choices.outcome: Poor and dishonest. Falsifying records turns a gap into misconduct.

choices.text: Fix the logs only, because the other gaps are paperwork.
choices.outcome: Partly right: log retention is important, but missed audit cycles and missing training evidence are breaches in their own right.

cards.title: The bank's IT reporting calendar with OJK
cards.caption: Plus yearly self-assessment of digital maturity (Art. 66) inside the IT condition report.

items.label: IT strategic plan
items.detail: Before the plan period starts (POJK 11 Art. 13).

items.label: IT development plan
items.detail: For the coming year; one change allowed by end of June (Art. 58).

items.label: IT condition report
items.detail: After year-end; PADK 1/2026 sets 21 January (Art. 59).

items.label: Cyber ratings and test results
items.detail: Inherent risk, maturity, risk level and vulnerability tests.

items.label: Scenario test report
items.detail: After the test report is complete (Art. 25).

items.label: Incidents
items.detail: Initial notice and incident report (Art. 60).

cards.back: Management oversight and control culture, risk assessment, segregation of duties, information systems, monitoring and correction.
The bank keeps audit trails of all IT activity for supervision, law enforcement, dispute resolution, verification and testing.
Based on need, priority and risk analysis, at least once a year.
Review of the IT internal audit function by an independent external party at least once every three years.
Results go to OJK within the reports set by OJK's internal audit rules.

cards.question: How often must the IT internal audit function be reviewed by an independent external party under POJK 11/2022?
options: Every year, with the internal audit
Only when OJK finds a problem
Every five years, with the IT strategic plan
At least once every three years
cards.explanation: Article 55(2) requires a review of the IT internal audit function at least once in three years by an independent external party. The IT internal audit itself runs at least once a year under Article 54(4).

cards.title: Real case: PADK 1/2026 replaces a nine-year-old circular
cards.body:
On **23 January 2026** OJK's Chief Executive of Banking Supervision set **PADK 1 of 2026** on IT operation by commercial banks, effective **1 March 2026**. It carries out fifteen articles of POJK 11/2022 and has four attachments: an IT operation **guide**, **procedures** for reports and permits, **report and notice formats**, and **permit and realisation formats**.

It **revoked SEOJK 21/2017** on IT risk management, which had guided banks since 2017. Among other things, it now spells out that the security policy includes **training and an awareness programme**, that **consultants, temporary staff and IT provider staff** receive security training or briefings by role, how **consent** and **impact assessments** for personal data work, and that banks already using IT providers must **align existing contracts** with it.

**Lesson:** a bank's policies, contracts and training must be updated when OJK's guidance changes, not at the next annual review.

cards.title: Build an evidence pack examiners can trust
cards.body:
- One **training register** by person (employee, consultant, temp, provider staff), topic, date and result.
- **Awareness programme** plan and the **phishing simulation** results with follow-up actions.
- **Audit** reports, findings and closure evidence; the **external review** of IT audit.
- **Test reports**, DR test results and incident files with notice times.
- **Consent** records and **impact assessments** for higher-risk processing.
- A map of which **policy clause** meets which OJK requirement.

cards.title: Stage five take-aways
items: Banks and affiliated parties keep depositor information secret; only listed exceptions apply, and deliberate disclosure is a crime.
Personal data processing needs explicit, purpose-specific consent and an impact assessment where risk rises.
IT internal audit runs at least yearly; its function is reviewed externally at least every three years; audit trails must exist.
Plans, the IT condition report, test results and incident reports each have OJK deadlines.
Evidence of role-based training for all people with access is part of being ready for OJK.

cards.prompt: If an OJK examiner asked you tomorrow to show how you protect customer data in your daily work, what evidence could you point to, and what is missing?

quiz.question: Under the Banking Law as amended by the P2SK Law, what does bank secrecy protect?
options: All information about every borrower and loan
Information about depositors and their deposits
Only the bank's internal salary data
Only information stored in electronic form
quiz.explanation: The amended law defines bank secrecy as information about depositors and their deposits, and Article 40 obliges banks and affiliated parties to keep it secret. Where a depositor is also a borrower, secrecy covers them as a depositor.

quiz.question: A lawyer phones a branch asking for a depositor's balance for a family dispute, with no court order and no written consent. What should staff do?
options: Decline, because none of the listed exceptions to bank secrecy applies
Disclose it, because lawyers are officers of the court
Disclose only the balance, not the transactions
Disclose it if the lawyer states the account number correctly
quiz.explanation: Article 40A lists the exceptions, such as court proceedings, the depositor's written request or consent, heirs, and tax rules. A phone request from a lawyer fits none of them, so the information stays secret.

quiz.question: What penalty does the amended Banking Law set for a bank employee who deliberately discloses protected depositor information?
options: A written warning from the bank's HR unit only
A fine of up to IDR 100 million with no prison term
Two to four years in prison and a fine of IDR 4 billion to IDR 8 billion
Dismissal, with no criminal liability
quiz.explanation: Article 47(2), as amended by the P2SK Law, sets imprisonment of two to four years and a fine of IDR 4 billion to 8 billion for directors, commissioners, employees or other affiliated parties who deliberately disclose such information.

quiz.question: Which consent design is in line with PADK 1/2026?
options: One pre-ticked box covering all current and future purposes
Consent implied when the customer keeps using the app
Consent to marketing required before an account can be opened
Separate unticked choices for each purpose, in plain language, with the right to withdraw explained
quiz.explanation: PADK 1/2026 rules out automatic or pre-ticked consent, asks for plain language, separate options for different purposes, information on the right to withdraw and refuse, and bars making unrelated consent a condition of service.

quiz.question: Marketing plans to track customers' locations through the mobile app. What does POJK 11/2022 require first?
options: An impact assessment on applying personal data protection principles
Approval from Bank Indonesia
A penetration test of the marketing team's laptops
Nothing, if customers accepted the app's terms
quiz.explanation: Article 44(2) requires an impact assessment where processing may raise risk for data owners; the elucidation lists tracking customers' location and behaviour as an example.

quiz.question: How often must a bank at least carry out an internal audit of IT operation under POJK 11/2022?
options: Once every three years
Once every two years
Once a year
Only when a significant incident occurs
quiz.explanation: Article 54(4) requires IT internal audit based on need, priority and risk, at least once a year. Every three years applies to the independent external review of the IT audit function.

quiz.question: Why must a bank keep audit trails of IT activity under POJK 11/2022?
options: Only to calculate staff overtime
To support supervision, law enforcement, dispute resolution, verification and testing
Only to meet tax filing rules
Only for marketing analytics
quiz.explanation: Article 54(2) requires audit trails of all IT activity for supervision, law enforcement, settling disputes, verification, testing and other examinations. Short log retention undermines this.

quiz.question: By when does PADK 1/2026 say the report on the current condition of IT operation for 2027 is due?
options: 30 November 2027
31 March 2028
30 June 2028
21 January 2028
quiz.explanation: POJK 11 Article 59 sets 15 working days after year-end, and PADK 1/2026 fixes the date as 21 January of the following year, giving the example of the 2027 report due by 21 January 2028. End of November is for plans.

quiz.question: A bank shares customers' transaction data with a fintech partner. Which document does PADK 1/2026 expect?
options: A data-exchange agreement covering scope, purpose, data types, roles, security and emergencies
A press release announcing the partnership
A single email from the partner promising care
OJK's prior written approval for each file sent
quiz.explanation: PADK 1/2026 asks for adequate cooperation agreements for data exchange with third parties, covering scope and duration, nature and purpose, data types, rights and duties of the parties, security and emergency exchange. POJK 11 Article 45 also requires customer consent to be considered.

quiz.question: Which record best proves to OJK that the bank met PADK 1/2026's training expectation for information security?
options: The vendor's marketing brochure about its training courses
Board minutes approving the training budget
A register showing role-based training or briefings for employees, consultants, temps and provider staff
A copy of OJK's regulation on the intranet
quiz.explanation: PADK 1/2026 expects training or briefings for all four groups by role. Only a record per person shows it happened; budgets and copies of rules show intent, not delivery.

regulators: Otoritas Jasa Keuangan (OJK, Financial Services Authority)

references.title: Peraturan Anggota Dewan Komisioner OJK Nomor 1 Tahun 2026 tentang Penyelenggaraan Teknologi Informasi oleh Bank Umum (OJK Board Member Regulation 1/2026 on IT operation by commercial banks)

references.note: The security policy covers training and an awareness programme; security training or briefings go to employees, consultants, temporary staff and IT provider staff by role. Also sets access control, incident handling, data protection and non-cyber incident reporting detail.

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 11/POJK.03/2022 tentang Penyelenggaraan Teknologi Informasi oleh Bank Umum (OJK Regulation 11/2022 on the use of information technology by commercial banks)

references.title: Peraturan Otoritas Jasa Keuangan Nomor 11/POJK.03/2022 tentang Penyelenggaraan Teknologi Informasi oleh Bank Umum (OJK Regulation 11/2022 on the use of information technology by commercial banks)

bank.question: A foreign bank branch in Jakarta argues POJK 11/2022 does not apply to it because its IT is run by head office abroad. Which answer is right?
options: It applies only to the branch's Indonesian-made systems
It does not apply if the home regulator supervises IT
It applies: POJK 11 defines commercial banks to include branches of banks based abroad
It applies only after OJK issues a specific instruction
bank.explanation: Article 1 defines a bank to include branch offices of banks domiciled abroad. Home supervision does not remove the duties, and offshore placement of systems needs OJK permission.

bank.question: Which pair correctly describes the IT roles of the Board of Directors and the Board of Commissioners under POJK 11/2022?
options: Directors set the IT strategic plan and policies; commissioners evaluate, direct and monitor the plan and IT governance
Commissioners set IT policies; directors only approve the budget
Both boards run the IT unit jointly day to day
Directors monitor; commissioners write the IT strategic plan
bank.explanation: Article 5 gives directors the IT strategic plan, policies, standards and procedures and monitoring of IT; Article 6 gives commissioners evaluation, direction and monitoring of the plan and of IT governance.

bank.question: An IT steering committee includes the IT director (chair), the head of the IT unit and the heads of two user units. What is missing under POJK 11/2022?
options: An independent commissioner
The head of internal audit
A representative of the IT provider
The director in charge of the risk management unit
bank.explanation: Article 7(3) requires at least the director over IT, the director over risk management, the head of the IT unit and the head of the IT user unit. Audit and providers are not required members.

bank.question: A bank plans to have an overseas provider process its card transactions outside Indonesia. What does POJK 11/2022 require?
options: Only notice to customers in the card terms
OJK permission, meeting conditions such as prudence, provider rules and keeping supporting documents in Indonesia
Only the provider's ISO certification
A Bank Indonesia licence instead of OJK's
bank.explanation: Article 39 keeps IT-based transaction processing in Indonesia, allowing processing by a provider abroad only with OJK permission and set conditions, including that supporting financial documents are kept at the bank's office in Indonesia.

bank.question: OJK grants a bank permission to place a group risk system in a data centre abroad. Eight months later the bank still has not moved it. What happens?
options: Nothing, permits have no deadline
The bank pays a daily fine until it moves
The permission lapses, because implementation was due within six months
OJK automatically extends the permit by a year
bank.explanation: Article 41 requires implementation within six months of permission; otherwise the permission is no longer valid.

bank.question: Which statement about OJK's IT rule set is accurate as of November 2026?
options: POJK 11/2022 is in force, implemented by PADK 1/2026, with SEOJK 29/2022 as the cyber circular
SEOJK 21/2017 is still the main IT risk guide
PADK 1/2026 revoked POJK 11/2022 and SEOJK 29/2022
POJK 38/2016 is still in force alongside POJK 11/2022
bank.explanation: PADK 1/2026 (from 1 March 2026) revoked only SEOJK 21/2017. POJK 11/2022 revoked POJK 38/2016 and its 2020 amendment. SEOJK 29/2022 still covers cyber resilience.

bank.question: Under POJK 11/2022, which aspect must a bank map and plan as part of IT governance, besides processes, structure and policies?
options: Shareholder dividend policy
Branch opening hours
The bank's advertising slogans
Supporting human resources and IT culture
bank.explanation: Article 3(1) lists business processes, organisation structure, policies, standards and procedures, information needs, supporting human resources, IT culture, and infrastructure and applications.

bank.question: A bank was warned in writing for not having an IT architecture and still has none. Which sanction can OJK impose next under POJK 11 Article 14?
options: A freeze on certain business activities
Personal imprisonment of the IT director
Compulsory merger with another bank
Suspension of all deposit insurance cover
bank.explanation: Article 14(2) provides a ban on new products, a freeze on certain activities and/or a lower governance factor in the soundness rating. Imprisonment, forced mergers and loss of deposit insurance are not administrative sanctions under POJK 11.

bank.question: According to its own preamble, why was PADK 1/2026 issued?
options: To replace the Banking Law's secrecy provisions
To carry out several articles of POJK 11/2022 and support continuity of bank IT operations and services
To regulate payment systems run by Bank Indonesia
To set rules only for Sharia business units
bank.explanation: PADK 1/2026 says it implements fifteen listed articles of POJK 11/2022 and supports continuity of operations and bank services that use IT. Payment systems are Bank Indonesia's field.

bank.question: A temporary staff member in IT support is given an administrator account with no signed acceptance of responsibility. Which PADK 1/2026 control is missing?
options: A yearly penetration test of the temp's computer
OJK approval of the temp's appointment
A disaster recovery test that includes the temp
A signed statement or agreement accepting responsibility for the user-ID and password when it is issued
bank.explanation: PADK 1/2026 says user-ID owners, especially employees, temporary staff and provider staff, sign a statement of responsibility or usage agreement when they receive the account and initial password or PIN.

bank.question: Which reason best explains why PADK 1/2026 asks banks to link role changes to access changes?
options: To reduce the number of software licences
Access must follow business need with minimum rights, so old rights are removed when duties change or end
To let staff keep useful access after transfers
To make audits shorter
bank.explanation: PADK 1/2026 bases access on business need with the least access possible, and requires procedures to change or close access when duties change or contracts end.

bank.question: A branch shares a network folder of customer files with no password. Which PADK 1/2026 rule applies?
options: File or folder sharing must at least be restricted by password or PIN and limited to authorised people
Shared folders are banned outright in all banks
Shared folders need OJK's permission
Only folders holding public data need protection
bank.explanation: PADK 1/2026 says banks using file or folder sharing must restrict access at least through a password or PIN and by setting who is authorised.

bank.question: Which example does PADK 1/2026 give of information classed as 'internal'?
options: Customer deposit data
Customer personal data
Internal rules on staff salaries
Product information offered to the public
bank.explanation: PADK 1/2026 gives deposit and personal data as 'secret', salary rules as 'internal' and product information as 'public'. Classification drives the protection each type gets.

bank.question: A provider employee notices he can open a system he should not have access to. Under PADK 1/2026, what is expected of him?
options: Use the access carefully until the contract ends
Tell only his own employer and wait
Post the weakness on a public forum to warn others
Report it to the bank's designated point of contact as a possible security incident
bank.explanation: PADK 1/2026 gives unauthorised access as an example of a security incident and expects employees, temporary staff and provider staff to report any sign of one to the point of contact. Banks may even consider rewarding such reports.

bank.question: PADK 1/2026 says the bank must set something for staff who break the information security policy. What is it?
options: A bonus scheme for compliant months
Sanctions for the violation
An automatic report to the police
A requirement to repeat induction only
bank.explanation: The policy must include sanctions for breaches, and the human resources procedure says the bank sets sanctions for violations of the security policy by staff.

bank.question: A system administrator role is being filled. HR proposes skipping background checks to save time. Which response fits PADK 1/2026?
options: Keep the checks: high-impact security roles need adequate controls before hiring
Skip them if the candidate has a university degree
Skip them for contract hires
Run them only after the probation period
bank.explanation: PADK 1/2026 expects adequate controls before employing permanent, contract or temporary IT staff, consultants or provider staff in positions with high security impact, giving criminal-record checks for network or system administrators as an example.

bank.question: A user forgets her password and the help desk resets it to 'Bank12345' for everyone. Which PADK 1/2026 expectation is broken?
options: Passwords must be at least twenty characters
Resets must be approved by OJK
Initial passwords should be unique, random, hard to guess and changed at first login
Passwords must contain only numbers
bank.explanation: PADK 1/2026 sets initial password or PIN controls: changed at first login, delivered securely, random and unique to each user, and not easy to guess. A shared standard reset password fails all of these.

bank.question: What does PADK 1/2026 allow a bank to consider to encourage staff to report security weaknesses?
options: Waiving training for staff who report
Publishing reporters' names in the press
Allowing reporters to test the weakness on live systems
Incentives for employees, temporary staff and provider staff who report exploitable incidents or weaknesses
bank.explanation: PADK 1/2026 says the bank may consider incentives for those who report IT incidents or vulnerabilities at risk of exploitation, to strengthen information security.

bank.question: A bank's IT team says penetration tests are optional because POJK 11 only says 'regularly'. Which reading is correct?
options: Testing is optional if no incident happened last year
Vulnerability-based testing is mandatory and periodic, with frequency set by the bank based on factors like criticality and change
Testing is needed only every five years
Only scenario tests are required; vulnerability tests are voluntary
bank.explanation: Article 24 requires vulnerability-based testing periodically; the elucidation and SEOJK 29 let the bank set frequency based on system criticality and changes, and expect penetration tests especially for banks with digital or online services.

bank.question: Which exercise does SEOJK 29/2022 describe as involving a red team and a blue team?
options: Adversarial attack simulation exercise
Table-top exercise
Business impact analysis
Vulnerability scan
bank.explanation: The adversarial attack simulation exercise uses real-world tactics; a red team attacks and a blue team detects, prevents and responds. A table-top is discussion-based.

bank.question: A bank hires a third party to run its scenario-based cyber test. What does SEOJK 29/2022 require?
options: Transfer responsibility for the test to the third party
Ask OJK to appoint the third party
Keep the results secret from the directors
Ensure the third party is competent, for example through recognised certification, and stay responsible for the test
bank.explanation: The circular allows testing in-house or by third parties, but the bank must ensure adequate competence, shown for instance by certification or recognition, and remains responsible. Results go to the directors.

bank.question: Which SEOJK 29/2022 inherent-risk indicator relates to staff behaviour on devices?
options: The number of branches with air-conditioning
The bank's dividend payout ratio
The share of employees who access the bank's network through personal devices
The number of customers over sixty
bank.explanation: Among technology indicators the circular lists the number of employees with bring-your-own-device access and which applications personal devices can reach; more such access means higher inherent risk.

bank.question: What should a bank do with the results of its cyber security tests besides reporting them to OJK, according to SEOJK 29/2022?
options: Publish them on the bank's website
Give them to the directors as a basis to improve governance, controls and staff capacity and awareness
Share them with all customers by email
Delete them after OJK receives the report
bank.explanation: The circular says test results go to the directors as the basis for improving governance, policies, internal control, and staff capacity and awareness, and that results must be documented and kept confidential.

bank.question: Who should take part in a scenario-based cyber test according to SEOJK 29/2022?
options: Relevant parties including executives, business and corporate communications, the crisis team, providers and technical staff
Only the cyber unit's own analysts
Only the external testers
Only OJK supervisors
bank.explanation: The circular says the bank must involve relevant parties, including executive officers, business functions, corporate communications, the crisis management team, service providers and technical staff responsible for detection, response and recovery.

bank.question: Which task does SEOJK 29/2022 give to the cyber resilience and security unit?
options: Approving the IT budget on behalf of the directors
Operating the core banking system day to day
Auditing the internal audit function
Coordinating or carrying out the resilience processes, cyber self-assessments, the risk level and cyber testing
bank.explanation: The circular lists coordination or execution of the four resilience processes, inherent risk and maturity self-assessments, setting the cyber risk level and cyber testing; the unit is independent of IT operations.

bank.question: A bank's phishing simulation shows a high click rate in one region. Which follow-up best matches SEOJK 29/2022?
options: Dismiss everyone who clicked
Stop running simulations to protect morale
Use a gap analysis of staff knowledge to plan targeted capacity building and update the awareness programme
Report each clicker's name to OJK
bank.explanation: The circular expects a gap analysis of staff cyber knowledge to drive capacity plans, and an awareness programme reviewed and updated for current threats. It does not ask for names to OJK.

bank.question: What does SEOJK 29/2022 say about the awareness programme's delivery methods?
options: It must be a single e-learning course set by OJK
It can use seminars, discussions, workshops and spreading cyber security policies and procedures
It must be delivered only by external trainers
It must be held only in English
bank.explanation: The criteria give seminars, discussions, workshops and dissemination of policies and procedures as examples, run at least yearly and kept up to date. No single OJK course is prescribed.

bank.question: Which of these is an example of a cyber incident given in POJK 11/2022's elucidation?
options: Web defacement that changes the bank's website content
A teller's arithmetic error at the counter
A late salary payment
A customer forgetting a PIN
bank.explanation: The elucidation lists hacking, viruses, malware, ransomware, web defacement and distributed denial of service attacks as causes of cyber incidents.

bank.question: A non-cyber incident, a failed overnight batch, stopped transfers for six hours and drew negative press. Is it reportable?
options: No: only cyber attacks are reportable
No: only losses above a fixed rupiah threshold count
Only if a customer files a formal complaint
Yes: a non-cyber incident with significant disruption or non-financial loss such as reputational harm must be reported
bank.explanation: Article 60 covers IT incidents, cyber and non-cyber, that cause or may cause significant loss or disrupt operations. Loss includes non-financial loss such as negative news; PADK 1/2026 sets the non-cyber procedure.

bank.question: Another authority gives a bank three working days for initial notice of a cyber incident. Which deadline applies for OJK?
options: Three working days, matching the other authority
OJK's own 24-hour deadline, because the other rule is slower
Whichever the bank prefers
Five working days for both notice and report
bank.explanation: SEOJK 29 and PADK 1/2026 say that when another authority's deadline is longer, the bank follows POJK 11: initial notice within 24 hours and report within 5 working days.

bank.question: What must an initial incident notice to OJK contain?
options: A completed root-cause analysis
The final cost of the incident
The initial information available about the incident, in OJK's set format
Approval from the bank's commissioners
bank.explanation: The initial notice is based on the information available and uses the circular's or PADK's format; the fuller incident report follows within five working days with more complete information.

bank.question: A bank's main IT provider is acquired and reorganised. What does POJK 11/2022 require?
options: Reassess the provider's materiality after the significant organisational change
Nothing until the contract expires
Automatically terminate the contract
Ask OJK to audit the provider first
bank.explanation: Article 31 requires a materiality reassessment when the provider's organisation changes significantly; Article 32 then lists conditions that require reporting and action.

bank.question: Before ending an IT provider contract early, what must the bank do under POJK 11/2022?
options: Notify customers 90 days in advance
Obtain the provider's written consent
Delete all data held by the provider at once
Prepare an exit plan, assess and test continuity of services and data, and ensure operations are not disrupted
bank.explanation: Article 32(4) requires a termination plan, an assessment of service and data continuity with testing or simulation, and assurance that ending the arrangement does not disrupt the bank.

bank.question: Which disaster recovery test meets POJK 11/2022?
options: A yearly test of one non-critical application chosen at random
A yearly test of all critical applications and infrastructure from the business impact analysis, involving IT users
A desk review of the plan with no testing
A test every three years run only by the IT unit
bank.explanation: Article 18(3) requires testing at least yearly on all critical applications and infrastructure per the business impact analysis, with IT users involved; Article 18(4) adds a yearly review.

bank.question: Why does SEOJK 29/2022 ask the bank to make sure its initial notice has been received by OJK?
options: Because the bank, not the supervisor, must make sure the notice actually arrives in time
Because OJK replies with a fine notice
Because receipt starts the five-working-day clock
Because OJK must approve the notice before the bank can act
bank.explanation: The circular asks banks to make efforts to ensure OJK has received the initial notice. The five-working-day clock runs from when the bank became aware of the incident, not from receipt.

bank.question: During a ransomware attack the response team copies infected server data onto a USB stick without any chain of custody. What does PADK 1/2026 expect instead?
options: Wipe the servers immediately to stop the spread
Let the provider take the servers away for repair
Pay the ransom quickly to limit downtime
Collect and preserve information meant as digital evidence using forensically sound methods
bank.explanation: PADK 1/2026 says that where information may become digital evidence, its collection and preservation must be done in a digitally forensically sound way, after documenting and isolating affected systems.

bank.question: Who must keep confidential depositor information that the bank has lawfully disclosed under an exception, according to the amended Banking Law?
options: Only the bank's employees
Nobody, once it has left the bank
Every person who obtains the information
Only OJK staff
bank.explanation: Article 40C, inserted by the P2SK Law, requires every person who obtains depositor information through the listed exceptions to keep it confidential.

bank.question: A customer is both a depositor and a borrower. What does the amended Banking Law require?
options: Nothing is secret, because borrowing removes secrecy
Keep secret the information about the customer in their capacity as a depositor
Keep everything secret, including the loan, in all cases
Disclose the deposit to any lender who asks
bank.explanation: Article 40(2) says that where a depositor is also a borrower, the bank and affiliated parties keep secret the information about the customer as a depositor.

bank.question: Which situation does POJK 11/2022's elucidation list as a trigger for a personal data impact assessment?
options: Sending a monthly account statement
Printing a deposit slip
Answering a customer's balance enquiry
Processing sensitive data on ethnicity, religion, race or inter-group relations
bank.explanation: The elucidation of Article 44(2) lists new technology, tracking location and behaviour, large-scale monitoring of public places, and processing sensitive data on ethnicity, religion, race and inter-group relations.

bank.question: What must a personal data protection impact assessment contain, according to PADK 1/2026?
options: A description and purpose of processing, a necessity and proportionality test, a risk assessment for data subjects and safeguards
Only the cost of the new system
Only the customer's signature
Only the vendor's marketing claims
bank.explanation: PADK 1/2026 lists a description and purpose of processing including the bank's interest, a necessity and proportionality assessment, a risk assessment for data subjects' rights and steps to protect them.

bank.question: What does PADK 1/2026 say about appointing someone for personal data protection?
options: The bank must appoint an OJK-certified officer for every branch
Only the IT provider may hold the role
The bank may appoint an official or officer to ensure data protection principles are applied, considering competence
The role is banned because it duplicates compliance
bank.explanation: PADK 1/2026 says the bank can appoint an official or officer responsible for applying personal data protection principles, chosen with regard to competence. It is an option in that text, not a per-branch duty.

bank.question: What does PADK 1/2026 say about consent to things unrelated to the customer's service?
options: It must be collected before any account opens
It must not be made a condition for providing the bank's service
It may be implied from silence
It may be bundled with the terms and conditions
bank.explanation: PADK 1/2026 says the bank does not make consent to matters not directly related to the customer a precondition for its services, and gives customers the right to refuse or withdraw.

bank.question: By what date must a bank submit its IT development plan for the coming year, and how often may it change it under the normal route?
options: By 21 January each year; unlimited changes
Within 15 working days of year-end; two changes
By the end of March; no changes allowed
By the end of November before the plan year; one change by the end of June
bank.explanation: Article 58 requires the IT development plan by end of November before the plan year and allows at most one change by the end of June; other changes need OJK approval.

bank.question: How often must a bank self-assess its digital maturity under POJK 11/2022, and where is it reported?
options: At least once a year, reported as part of the report on the current condition of IT operation
Every three years, in a separate letter to the commissioners
Only when launching a digital bank
Monthly, in the bank's financial statements
bank.explanation: Article 66 requires a periodic digital maturity self-assessment at least once a year, reported within the IT condition report.

bank.question: An OJK examiner asks how the bank knows its IT internal audit is effective. Which evidence best answers under POJK 11/2022?
options: The IT unit's own statement that audits are fine
A list of IT audit staff and their salaries
The independent external review of the IT audit function within the last three years and audit results reported to OJK
The bank's annual advertising report
bank.explanation: Article 55 requires an IT internal audit guide, an independent external review of the function at least every three years, and reporting of review and audit results to OJK.
